<DOCUMENT id="aml/structuring.md">Structuring is the deliberate act of breaking a single large cash transaction into multiple smaller transactions, each below a mandatory reporting threshold, to avoid a report. The rule fires when aggregated same-customer cash credits exceed 90% of the threshold across a rolling 72-hour window while no single transaction breaches it.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT id="card/friendly-fraud.md">Friendly fraud occurs when a genuine cardholder falsely disputes a legitimate purchase.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT id="aml/smurfing.md">Smurfing uses many individuals who each conduct sub-threshold transactions on behalf of a controller.</DOCUMENT>

Question: A customer made five cash deposits of 9,400 units over two days, none above the 10,000 threshold. Name the typology and the rule.

##Reason: The deposits come from a single customer, are each engineered just below the 10,000 reporting threshold, and aggregate well above it within 72 hours. That is one actor splitting their own transaction to evade reporting — structuring, not smurfing (which needs many actors) and not layering (which obscures origin regardless of amount). The structuring rule cited in aml/structuring.md fires when aggregated same-customer cash exceeds 90% of the threshold across a rolling 72-hour window with no single breach, which is met here. ##Answer: Typology: structuring. The structuring monitoring rule is breached (aggregate same-customer cash > 90% of the 10,000 threshold within 72 hours, no single transaction over the line). Escalate to SAR readiness review; human approval required before filing.

<DOCUMENT id="aml/smurfing.md">Smurfing is the use of multiple people who each conduct sub-threshold transactions on behalf of a controlling party. The rule fires when three or more distinct customers credit a common beneficiary with sub-threshold cash within a rolling 7-day window.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT id="aml/structuring.md">Structuring is one actor splitting their own transaction below a reporting threshold.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT id="kyc/kyc-refresh.md">KYC refresh is the periodic re-verification of customer identity.</DOCUMENT>

Question: Four unrelated individuals each deposited 8,000 units toward one beneficiary account within a week. What typology is this and which rule fired?

##Reason: The distinguishing feature is many distinct individuals moving sub-threshold amounts toward one beneficiary, which is smurfing rather than structuring (a single actor). aml/smurfing.md gives the rule: three or more distinct customers crediting a common beneficiary with sub-threshold cash within a rolling 7-day window. Four customers over one week meets it. ##Answer: Typology: smurfing. The smurfing rule is breached (≥3 distinct customers crediting one beneficiary with sub-threshold cash within 7 days; here four within a week). Escalate to SAR readiness review; human approval required.
